concept: Mitiq ZNE is a mitigation wrapper, not a state-evolution method
summary: Mitiq zero-noise extrapolation acts around a circuit executor and observable workflow, requiring repeated executions at scaled noise levels; in OpenQEvo it should remain a non-executable planned wrapper until an adapter defines how to connect base evolution circuits, executors, and observables.
limitations: ZNE mitigates noise in measured observables but does not remove algorithmic product-formula error.
It requires additional executions and shot budget across noise scale factors.
It requires a compatible executor and observable interface, which OpenQEvo does not yet register as an executable method.
implications: Do not recommend mitiq_zne as an executable OpenQEvo evolution method yet.
Recommend Mitiq only as a planned mitigation layer around a base circuit-based evolution strategy.
If implemented later, the method contract must include base method, executor, observable, scale factors, and extrapolation factory.

evidence.note: Documents the ZNE workflow concepts and use cases.
Documents execute_with_zne, extrapolation factories, and noise-scaling helpers.
